Volumes and green weight

Source: vignettes/volumes-scaling.Rmd
volumes-scaling.Rmd

stem_volume() measures bounded stem sections, and tree_cubic_volume() measures above the stump without product specifications. green_weight() converts cubic volume to short tons for merchandising.

## Select example trees
trees <- example_trees %>%
  slice_head(n = 3)

## Measure a section inside bark
section <- stem_volume(dbh = trees$dbh,
                       ht = trees$ht,
                       spcd = trees$spcd,
                       lower = 1,
                       lower_type = 'height',
                       upper = 32,
                       upper_type = 'height')
volume (cubic feet) status
14.556 0
22.879 0
28.230 0

Bounds may be heights, inside or outside bark diameters, the stump, or the tip. inside_bark selects the volume basis.

## Measure each tree above the stump
volume <- tree_cubic_volume(dbh = trees$dbh,
                            ht = trees$ht,
                            spcd = trees$spcd,
                            stump_ht = 1,
                            top_dib = 6)
volume (cubic feet) status
15.003 0
26.626 0
37.564 0

Omitting top_dib measures to the tip. The top diameter stays inside bark when inside_bark = FALSE.

Green weight

The default converts inside bark volume to green wood and attached bark weight using species properties.

## Convert stem volume to green short tons
weight <- green_weight(volume = volume$value,
                       spcd = trees$spcd)
green weight (short tons) status
0.353 0
0.678 0
0.883 0

component, moisture, and the physical property overrides control the conversion. inside_bark = FALSE accepts volume including bark.

Trim

A log occupies its nominal length plus trim, is scaled on its nominal length, and leaves the trim wood as a residual.

## Define saw specifications
saw <- product(product = 'domestic_saw',  ## product name, unitless
               min_length = 16,  ## feet
               max_length = 40,  ## feet
               trim = 1,  ## feet
               min_sed = 6,  ## inches
               volume_unit = 'scribner')  ## Scribner board feet

## Cut logs with trim
result <- merchandise(tree_id = trees$tree,
                      dbh = trees$dbh,
                      ht = trees$ht,
                      spcd = trees$spcd,
                      products = saw)
tree_id log product start_height (feet) end_height (feet) length (feet) scaling_length (feet) sed (inches) led (inches) scaling_diameter (inches) inside_bark scale (Scribner board feet) volume_unit
1 1 domestic_saw 1 34 32 32 6.024 13.012 6 TRUE 50 scribner
2 1 domestic_saw 1 42 40 40 6.541 14.897 7 TRUE 70 scribner
3 1 domestic_saw 1 42 40 40 8.830 17.097 9 TRUE 120 scribner
tree_id from (feet) to (feet) cause
1 33 34 trim
2 41 42 trim
3 41 42 trim

Scaling rules control how nominal lengths and diameters enter the selected scale.
